title: Catpilot organization overlay, version 2
description: Version 2 of the company rules file (docs/spec/OVERLAY_V2.md). Every model-facing list item is an object with a stable id and its phrase as text; an optional machine-only enforcement section holds rules that are never rendered into a prompt or returned by the server; optional topic contacts name who to ask about data, hosting, services or identity, with owner as the default. Version 1 files are checked against overlay.schema.json instead. A file with enforcement also carries a random salt, so the file's SHA-256, which a model sees, cannot confirm a guessed enforcement value. Cross-field rules are checked by tools/validate_overlay.py only, as in version 1: ids, aliases and template kinds unique across the file, use_instead resolving to an approved item, no enforcement host in a model-facing value, the secret and content scans (which allow an email address only in owner and a contact's name, and check a contact's intake_url as intake_url), and IP addresses refused as hosts. Never commit an overlay to a public repository.

organization.description: Display name only. No internal identifiers, tenant IDs, or domains.

owner.description: Where 'ask a human' points: a team mailbox, channel name, or role. One value.

intake_url.description: Optional HTTPS intake form URL for security review requests. No credentials, no query string, host on the validator's allowlist.

contacts.description: Optional topic contacts (OVERLAY_V2.md §3.1), one per check_plan field that has a topic: data (data_classes), hosting, services, identity (audience). check_plan names the contact for the field that decided its outcome; a tie between fields, write_access and any other case use owner, which stays the default. Model-facing: rendered into the rules block and returned by list_approved("contacts").

reviewed_on.description: Date a named reviewer accepted these values.

expires_on.description: After this date the values are treated as unknown; a private bundle cannot be built from an expired overlay.

location.description: HTTPS only, no credentials, no query string, host on the validator's allowlist. Omit if the tool cannot reach it.

salt.description: Machine-only. A random value of 32 to 128 lowercase hex characters, required with enforcement (OVERLAY_V2.md §6.3 rule 10). Set one with: python tools/validate_overlay.py salt FILE. The example's value is rejected here; the validator also rejects salts close to it and other hand-made ones (well-known published values, repeated or evenly stepping patterns, fewer than 8 different digits, runs of consecutive digits).

enforcement.description: Machine-only. Never rendered into a prompt or returned by the server; read by hooks and the pull-request check once they ship. Validated only in this release.

default_mode.description: The mode of a rule with no mode of its own.

name.description: Follows the owner rules: a team mailbox, channel name, or role. An email address is allowed here, as in owner.

intake_url.description: Optional HTTPS intake form URL for this topic, following the intake_url rules: no credentials, no query string, host on the validator's allowlist. The escalation draft uses it in place of the file's intake_url.

id.description: Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens. Unique across the file: item ids, aliases, template kinds and enforcement rule ids; never reused for a different thing.

phrase.description: One short phrase. No URLs, no email addresses, no secrets, no narrative, no enforcement value.

aliases.description: Former ids, matched exactly; not synonyms.

kind.description: Closed list (OVERLAY_V2.md §2.2). Each kind entered the schema with its first consumer, the company-rules hook.

use_instead.description: The id or an alias of an item in hosting.approved or services.approved.

branch.description: A Git branch name: no spaces, .., ~, ^, :, ?, [, \ or leading -; * only as a trailing /*, which covers the prefix.

host.description: A lowercase host name with at least one dot, optionally starting with *. to cover subdomains. No scheme, port, path, credentials or IP address.

registry.description: A host name as for deploy_host, optionally followed by a path of letters, digits, ., _, - and /, with no . or .. segment; at most 255 characters, the compiled policy's limit. No scheme, port, query or credentials.

cloud_account.description: aws:<12 digits>, azure:<lowercase subscription GUID> or gcp:<project id: 6 to 30 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter>.
